content:
General Motors first announced back in 2023 that it would drop CarPlay from all its future electric vehicles, and later offered a series of absurd justifications, even hinting at one point that doing so was Steve Jobs' wish.

However, it now looks like an exception may be emerging. The original policy shift was made based on customer feedback, and it seems GM may now need to revisit its decision...

Engadget spotted the report from CarBuzz.

Cadillac's online configurator has opened up for several 2027 models, and we noticed that the Lyriq still comes standard with CarPlay and Android Auto. The Lyriq is Cadillac's first all-electric vehicle and also a tech-oriented model, which we believe is steadily becoming one of the best luxury EVs. A Cadillac representative told CarBuzz: "Cadillac will continue to refine its infotainment strategy across the entire EV lineup based on customer feedback, while also prioritising the in-vehicle native experience."

Further reading: We discovered that without CarPlay, consumers simply won't buy luxury EVs.

Engadget also mentioned a practical workaround for owners of other GM vehicles that don't support CarPlay.

Is GM's plan to abandon CarPlay finally coming to an end? Share your thoughts in the comments.
